description: Follow-up on WO #400074. Investigating JCI VA-7452-90011 electric valve actuator on hot water reheat coil. Actuator appeared reverse acting: 100% command was closing the valve, 0% was opening. Diagnosed jumper configuration — JP5 (DA/RA action) was already bridged/IN = Direct Acting. JP6 (fail-safe) already set to PDTO (fail-closed). Flipped JP5 to RA to test theory. Power cycled actuator — spring returned to fully open, no calibration stroke observed. At 100% command (RA = close), valve still not closing all the way. Root cause identified: common wire was disconnected at actuator terminals. Floating common caused erratic signal behavior and explained original reverse-acting appearance.

action: Reconnected common wire on JCI VA-7452-90011 actuator terminals. During diagnosis, JP5 jumper was flipped from DA to RA for testing.
outcome: System restored after common wire reconnected. Floating common was root cause of erratic actuator behavior. Verify final JP5 jumper position (DA vs RA) matches sequence of operations — confirm valve responds correctly: 0% = closed, 100% = open on DA. Power cycle actuator after any final jumper changes to force recalibration.
